grounds.locator: Diagnostics and the weak-definite boundary cases

projection.target: The keys normally identifies an accessible set and can supply a domain in two of the keys. The radio in Jo listened to the radio can still have a conventional activity reading without identifying one physical radio.
projection.evidence: CGEL documents both ordinary definites and restricted non-referential readings. Reynolds uses partitive domain establishment as a structural test rather than relying on identifiability alone.

curious.title: Phrases that point to a particular thing
curious.summary: Phrases like the dog, she or London can pick out something particular that the listener can work out.
curious.body: In The dog barked, the phrase the dog points to one particular dog that the listener can identify from the situation. The same kind of phrase can stand for a whole group the context makes clear, as in The students passed, or for the one person holding a role, as in The CEO resigned. It can also talk about a whole kind, as in The dodo is extinct. Not every use points to a single physical thing: in Jo listened to the radio, the phrase can have a conventional activity reading without picking out one particular radio.
curious.try: Say The dog barked to someone who doesn't know about any dog. What do they ask you?

teacher.summary: Lays out the meanings of definite NPs, from an identifiable referent to a role or a kind, and shows where they can be weaker.
teacher.explain: A definite NP consists of a definite determiner (the, this, that, a dependent genitive pronoun, or a genitive NP) with a nominal, or a referential personal pronoun, or a bare proper-name NP. The dictionary lists readings: an identifiable instance (The dog barked), a maximal set delimited by context (The students passed), a unique role (The CEO resigned), a kind (The dodo is extinct) and a generally characteristic property (The lion is dangerous). The keys normally identifies an accessible set and can supply a domain in two of the keys, but in Jo listened to the radio a conventional activity reading doesn't identify one radio. The dictionary marks this account as provisional.
teacher.terms: The is a determinative, often called the definite article. Weak definite is a name used for cases like the radio in Jo listened to the radio, which can have a conventional activity reading without identifying one physical radio.

contrasts.note: The indefinite alternative; the dog's identity is left unstated.

watch_for: A learner might think the has to point to one specific physical thing.
A learner might treat the dodo and the lion as naming one animal when they name a kind.
teacher.activity: Give students short story openings. They underline each definite NP and say what the listener is expected to identify (a thing, a group, a role or a kind).
